title: Brotherhood and Sisterhood
definition: Brotherhood and sisterhood is the spiritual family relationship believers share in Christ as members of God's household.
summary: Believers are brothers and sisters in Christ, called to love, honor, and care for one another.
christFocus: Jesus brings believers into the family of God and unites them as brothers and sisters through His saving work.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Brotherhood and sisterhood in Christ means believers are not isolated individuals but members of God's family. Through Christ, they share a new identity and responsibility toward one another.

This relationship calls for honor, affection, protection, correction, encouragement, generosity, and faithfulness. The Church should be a place where spiritual family is practiced, not merely named.

Because earthly families can be broken, the family of God becomes a deep place of belonging and care. Yet this family must reflect Christ, not repeat patterns of neglect, favoritism, or harm.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people come to Christ carrying loneliness, rejection, or family wounds. Brotherhood and sisterhood matters because the Church is called to embody the family love of God in practical ways.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Treat fellow believers as family in Christ. Encourage, protect, forgive, and serve them. Look especially for those who feel unseen or disconnected and draw them toward Gospel fellowship.
